week.worked: The cheap Arsenal end of the squad did the work: Calafiori and Tzolis returned fifteen of the thirty-one, and a £4.5m goalkeeper picked up a clean sheet in Brighton's 4-0. None of it was the plan.
week.didnt: The two most expensive decisions in the team produced nine points between them — the armband on a £15.5m striker in a City win, and a Manchester United triple that came home with five from a 2-0 defeat at Hull. Kerkez started at Newcastle and finished on nought.
week.next: Two of the eleven have not kicked a ball yet, so this is not a gameweek to draw conclusions from. There is nothing here that a transfer before Friday fixes; the United question belongs to GW4 at Old Trafford, and it should be left there.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Started at left-back for City on Sunday and returned nine. If the Kerkez seat is the one being questioned, this is the same money in a better defence.

watchlist.name: Dewsbury-Hall
watchlist.note: Eleven points from a £6.5m central midfielder in a 2-0 win. He is the honest replacement for Rogers if Chelsea's midfield stays unsettled — but wait for the Fulham line-up first.

week.worked: He was the only one of the five with a Brentford player, and he had two: Ajer at £4.5m and Schade returned eleven out of the 3-0 over Spurs. Szoboszlai added eight. The cheap end of his squad is the best-shaped in the room.
week.didnt: The captaincy and the goalkeeper both went to Manchester United on the day United lost at Hull — four from the armband, one from Lammens, and Mbeumo two on top of that. Three United assets in one afternoon, and eight points left on the bench.
week.next: The Brentford pair is a genuine edge nobody else has, and it is cheap enough to keep through Leeds. The exposure is the same as Xabi's — three United men — but with a goalkeeper on top, which is the version that hurts more when the defence concedes headers.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: Fourteen on debut, and a third Brentford asset in the price range where he is already right. If the defensive contributions repeat, this is a cheaper edge than Schade.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Eleven points at £6.5m. He owns Calafiori and no Arsenal attacker; that was the shape that cost the room the most this weekend.

week.worked: The mid-price picks were the best in the room: Ndiaye, Szoboszlai and Calafiori returned twenty-six between them, all bought between £5.5m and £7.0m. He is fourth in the league and the only gaffer in the top four without a chip spent.
week.didnt: Twelve points on the bench, nine of them Gvardiol — a starting City defender left out for Hume, who Sunderland then played out of position at right wing. That is the largest bench score of the five and the one that was avoidable at the deadline rather than after it.
week.next: Nothing about the squad needs fixing; the ordering does. Gvardiol started against Bournemouth and started at left-back — that is a pick to trust ahead of a £4.5m defender whose own manager has been moving him up the pitch.

watchlist.name: Guéhi
watchlist.note: Ten points on his first City start, in for the reshuffle after Doku's injury. Worth watching only until Kovacic and Doku are back and the XI settles.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: Eight points off the bench. The return arrived, the start did not — and a substitute is not a seat. Doku is out until 5 September, so the window to prove it is now.

week.worked: Two Arsenal picks nobody else in the room owns — Havertz and Mosquera — returned twelve from about £13m of squad, and Tzolis added six. He found the Arsenal exposure the rest of the five were missing, just not in the attack.
week.didnt: He triple-upped on City and got six for it, and one of the three, Aït-Nouri, was on the bench at the Etihad while Gvardiol played left-back. Semenyo at £8.5m is his second-priciest outfielder and returned two. Palestra started nothing because Chelsea have not played.
week.next: Seventh with three players still to play is not a position, it is a queue. The line-up sheet is the thing to read here, not the scoreline: a City defender who is on the bench in GW1 is not likely to start in GW2 either.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: The player who kept Aït-Nouri out, for the same money. If the City defensive slot is worth owning, this is the one that plays.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: He already has the cheapest Arsenal defenders in the room; the eleven-point midfielder at £6.5m is the missing half of that bet.

week.worked: Top of the five and second in the league, and he would be top of the five without the chip — the eleven alone made thirty-nine. Ndiaye, Szoboszlai and Calafiori did most of it, which is three mid-price players rather than one lucky captain.
week.didnt: The Bench Boost, played in the first week of the season, returned six: two apiece from Kinsky, Diop and Groß, and nothing from Konsa. A record number of managers did the same thing, so this was the crowd's call rather than a lone one — but a chip that wants a double gameweek is gone in August, and he plays the rest of the first half one short. Cash cost him a point in a 4-0 defeat.
week.next: He leads on squad, not on chip, which is the good version of being ahead. The thing to watch is whether the six-point lead over the pack survives the first week where somebody else has a chip and he does not — and whether Villa's transfer noise makes Cash unplayable.

watchlist.name: Ajer
watchlist.note: Eight points, same price as Cash, in a side whose set pieces produced more shots than seven whole clubs managed on Saturday. The obvious swap if Villa keep selling.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: A first half without chips wants cheap ceiling. Fourteen on debut from a £5.5m midfielder is exactly that shape, if the defensive contributions hold.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Still nothing to say. Chelsea's season starts tonight at Fulham, so the ledger against Bruno has not opened and no verdict written about him this week would be honest.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: Hit the defensive-contribution threshold on debut despite coming off early, plus two assists and maximum bonus. One of the assists was a shot the goalkeeper parried into a teammate's path — the DefCon rate is the case, not the fourteen.

watchlist.name: Dewsbury-Hall
watchlist.note: Eleven points and the opener in Everton's 2-0. Cheap central midfielders in a side keeping clean sheets are the market the room is short of.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: The single biggest collective miss in the room: four of the five own an Arsenal defender, none owns the £6.5m midfielder who returned eleven.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: Eight from the bench with Doku out until 5 September. The trigger set last week was a start; it was not met, so this stays a watch rather than a buy.

watchlist.name: Woltemade
watchlist.note: Newcastle's penalty taker, in front of the kindest six-game run on the ticker — and a substitute at St James' Park with Osula leading the line. The fixtures are still right; the seat is not his.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes, the penalties, and a two-point opener that tells you nothing you had not already priced in at £15.5m.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury, or three straight weeks of City creating through the wide players and past him.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: Every minute, every set piece, every penalty — the problem at Hull was the side around him, not the player.
verdicts.trigger: A second blank against Ipswich at home, with United held to two big chances again, and the £12.0m becomes the hole rather than the price.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: Chelsea have not played, so nothing has happened and nothing has changed.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts as a ten, or a penalty converted, and he goes back to nailed. Two games wide and he is a sack.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Owned by all five and by 64% of the game, and still on nought purely because Chelsea's opener is tonight.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box and the 64% becomes the risk instead of the safety.

verdicts.name: Šeško
verdicts.why: Zero pre-season minutes became 23 at Hull, and the start still has not come.
verdicts.trigger: A start plus a goal and he re-enters as watch — but not before.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Started at left-back with Frimpong opposite him; the minutes were never the question, and a nought in a 2-2 is a scoreline, not a demotion.
verdicts.trigger: One week on the bench, or Liverpool moving to a back three, and the £5.5m stops making sense.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Nine points, owned by four of the five and by 40% of the game — the closest thing to a free lunch on the squad list.
verdicts.trigger: A recurrence of the knee trouble that has followed him around.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Six points deputising while both Saliba and Timber are out with no return date — the points are real, the seat is borrowed.
verdicts.trigger: Saliba's back clearing. When it does, this pick ends.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: Eleven points at £6.5m in the side that has looked most ready, and not one of the five owns him.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or Arsenal's returns concentrating in Saka and Gyökeres instead.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Six points at £7.5m with 6% ownership, in a forward line that has not yet settled around Gyökeres.
verdicts.trigger: Two weeks as a substitute once Arsenal's attack is fully fit.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Six more points and a debut that got noticed; the price still has not caught up.
verdicts.trigger: Saka and Rice fully fit squeezing the minutes.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Nine points and Arsenal's penalties at £9.5m, with under 10% of the game on him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or rotation through the Champions League weeks.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Alonso said the late World Cup returnees need time, and Chelsea's first line-up of the season is tonight.
verdicts.trigger: A bench at Craven Cottage makes Dewsbury-Hall a live GW3 move; a full ninety and he is solid again.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Leeds play through him and he started; a one-point opener is a dull floor, which is what he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or a striker arriving before the window shuts.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Central midfield at Newcastle, on Liverpool's penalties, at £7.0m — and 42% of the game is already there, so the differential case is gone.
verdicts.trigger: A shift back to right-back under the new manager and the appeal halves.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: Twelve points at £7.0m with under 4% ownership, but there is transfer noise around him and Liverpool's front line is not settled.
verdicts.trigger: A second start and a second return before the window closes.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Nine points on Everton's penalties at £6.0m, in a side that opened with a clean sheet — two of the five already have him.
verdicts.trigger: Everton's fixtures turning, or the penalty duty moving.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes and the opener in a 2-0, from a £6.5m central midfielder in a side keeping clean sheets.
verdicts.trigger: A second blank in three with Everton conceding, and he goes back to being a hedge.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Started at left-back and returned nine — the City defensive seat that actually exists at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: O'Reilly reclaiming the left side once Doku is back on 5 September.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Ten points on his first City start, in a back line reshuffled around Doku's injury rather than by design.
verdicts.trigger: One week out of the XI with Dias and Khusanov fit and the £6.0m is wrong.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Eight points from the bench. The trigger written last week was a start, and he did not get one.
verdicts.trigger: A start while Doku is out. Another cameo, however productive, is not evidence of a seat.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: Two points at £8.5m from a starting City wide player — the price assumes returns the role has not yet produced.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks with Cherki and Marmoush getting minutes and this is a sack.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: Fourteen on debut, but the case is the defensive-contribution rate, not the two assists — one of which was a parried shot.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks over the DefCon threshold and he is the £5.5m midfielder of the season. One is a debut.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Eight points at £4.5m in a Brentford side that had more set-piece shots on Saturday than seven clubs managed in total.
verdicts.trigger: Collins or Kayode taking the aerial returns instead, or one rotation.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: A game-high five second-half shots and a penalty won in a 3-0 — the underlying numbers are ahead of the three points.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks of shot volume without a return and the finishing becomes the story.

verdicts.name: Thiago
verdicts.why: Missed from the spot after scoring ten of his previous eleven, blanked in a 3-0 win, and Brentford's run turns hard from GW5.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties to anyone, and the £8.0m is a sack the same day.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Two points, but the shape of the problem at Hull was the team's, and 38% of the game is not moving yet.
verdicts.trigger: United blanking again at home to Ipswich, which would make the GW4 sell decision automatic.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: A £4.5m defender in a back line that conceded two headed set plays to a promoted side.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three restores him; another set-piece collapse and the cheap seat is not worth the slot.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Cheap is not the same as safe behind a defence that lost 2-0 at Hull to two headers.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in the next three, or enough save points to make the floor worth it.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: One point, and he is the defender in the middle of the set plays United conceded.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-back options are fit.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: A clean sheet in a 4-0 at £4.5m, which is the entire job description of this pick.
verdicts.trigger: Steele getting a cup start that turns into a league one.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Spurs did not have a shot on target until 3-0 down, and their manager said the side is not in the right physical condition.
verdicts.trigger: Scout's line is GW7 — window shut, players back, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Minus one in a 4-0, in a Villa side that left out its goalkeeper and its striker over transfer uncertainty.
verdicts.trigger: Villa selling Watkins or Martínez outright, and this becomes a sack the same week.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland pushed him forward into a right-wing role — good for the assists, bad for the clean sheets he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: A second week out of the back line. A £4.5m defender who does not defend is priced wrong for the position.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Plenty of the ball and Sunderland going through him, but no shots and no chances created.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the £6.0m goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Emersonn
verdicts.why: Nine points, three shots and the best xGI of any Ipswich player at £5.5m — a genuinely cheap forward with a role.
verdicts.trigger: One start on the bench once Ipswich's four attacking signings settle.

signals.text: City's confirmed XI against Bournemouth had Gvardiol at left-back and Aït-Nouri among the substitutes. Maresca made two changes from the Community Shield: Rico Lewis in for the benched Kovacic, and Guéhi in for the injured Doku, with O'Reilly pushed into a more advanced role.
signals.action: if you own Aït-Nouri you own a substitute — Gvardiol is the City left-back until a line-up says otherwise

signals.text: Meunier's return from injury pushed Hume forward into an out-of-position right-wing slot, something Sunderland used repeatedly in pre-season. He blanked but should have had an assist — Opta classed two of the chances he created as big chances.
signals.action: reprice him: the ceiling went up and the clean-sheet floor went down, which is the wrong trade for a £4.5m defender slot

signals.text: O'Nien started at centre-half only because Mukiele and Alderete had pre-season fitness issues. He gave the ball away for Ipswich's opener, was booked for a tactical foul, and was replaced by Alderete midway through the second half.
signals.action: the £4.0m Sunderland defender is not a seat — expect a change from the start next weekend

signals.text: Hit the defensive-contribution threshold on debut despite coming off early, added two assists and maximum bonus for fourteen. Scout's caveat: one assist was a shot from outside the box that Kinsky parried into Kayode's path — the difference between an eight-point return and a fourteen.
signals.action: buy the DefCon rate if it repeats, not the fourteen; two more weeks over the threshold is the evidence

signals.text: Missed a penalty in the 3-0 win over Spurs after converting ten of his previous eleven. He also headed against the bar and went close at the near post; the front three all blanked in a three-goal win.
signals.action: the miss is noise, the run from GW5 — Chelsea, Villa, Liverpool — is not; if the spot-kick duty moves, sell that day

signals.text: Spurs did not register a shot on target until 3-0 down, with an xG of 3.96-0.47 against. De Zerbi: "For sure, we are not in the right physical condition for a lot of reasons. For the players, they came late after the World Cup." Scout reckon perhaps three of that XI will still be starting come the autumn.
signals.action: GW7 is the reassess point — window shut, players back, fixtures softer. Until then, target Spurs rather than own them

signals.text: Newcastle's confirmed XI at St James' Park had Osula leading the line and Wissa behind him, with Woltemade on the bench.
signals.action: hold off — the £6.0m penalty taker in front of the best six-game run on the ticker is not currently starting

signals.text: Superb on his second Ipswich debut — an assist, three efforts — before limping off. O'Neil: "Thankfully, it's just cramp. We need to get him up to speed with the rest of the lads because our boys have been through a tough pre-season."
signals.action: the 75% flag in the game is fitness, not damage; read the GW2 line-up rather than the flag

signals.text: A record number of FPL managers played the Bench Boost in Gameweek 1.
signals.action: context for the chip already spent in this league: it was the crowd's call, not one person's — which makes it a cheaper mistake, not a smaller one

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week, not against the table. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used — and the manager who played it still leads, which is the point: the chip was not the reason.
Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on the bench or out of position.

plan.outlook: Eighth of eleven on 31, Arsene second on 45, the league leader on 57 — and none of it is settled, because Chelsea are at Fulham tonight and every one of the five is still waiting on João Pedro. The gameweek turned on three things nobody chose deliberately: Arsenal's cheap defenders paying, the Manchester United triple-ups failing at Hull, and both captaincy options — Haaland and Bruno — returning two points each, which means the armband separated nobody at all. Four of the five sit within eight points of one another; the fifth got clear and spent a chip to do part of it. There is no transfer this week that would survive being written down. The three real decisions are all later: whether the United block survives GW4 at Old Trafford, whether the whole room is underweight Arsenal's midfield, and whether anyone else is tempted to spend a chip in August.

items.label: GW1 settles
items.note: the last fixture of the gameweek, and it holds two or three players in every squad in this league. The log settles after it, and so does the roast

items.label: GW2 deadline
items.note: no move recommended. The Hull defenders are all flagged at 75%, Sangaré has played one game, and the two best mid-price adds — Ødegaard and Gvardiol — are each worth a week of confirmation

items.label: The United question
items.note: three United men run into City at Old Trafford, and four of the five are exposed to it. Ipswich at home in GW2 is the evidence; the sale, if there is one, is GW4

items.label: Wildcard
items.note: hold through the first international break — that is when the market misprices and the data is real. Arsene now plays that window one chip lighter than everyone else

rows.name: Wildcard
rows.window: earliest sensible window GW6–8 — post-break, once real data exists

rows.name: Free Hit
rows.window: hold for a blank gameweek; none scheduled yet

rows.name: Bench Boost
rows.window: wants a clean double gameweek; none scheduled yet

rows.name: Triple Captain
rows.window: a premium on a home double, or not at all

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). A good week used beats a perfect week hoarded — but Gameweek 1, when every squad is fifteen fit players and there are no doubles anywhere, is neither. One of the five has already found that out, for six points.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Arsene's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.
